replication_study.hypothesis: Among sampled U.S. counties, a higher 2016 Trump vote share is associated with a smaller percentage-point increase in the proportion of residents staying home, conditional on socioeconomic, demographic, employment, rurality, age, and state fixed effects.

data_plan.dataset_identifier: Supplied county_variables.csv and transportation.csv replication dataset
data_plan.source_type: County-level election, socioeconomic, demographic, industry, rurality, and anonymized mobility data
data_plan.wave_or_subset: A deterministic 5% county sample (seed 2982); reference dates February 16–29, 2020; primary March dates March 19–April 1, 2020; later comparison August 16–29, 2020.
data_plan.sample_size: 5% of 3,142 counties selected before listwise deletion; the final analytic N is saved in results/results.json.
data_plan.access_details: Input CSV files are supplied in task_input/replication_data.

qualification.explanation: The supplied data allow the same county-level observational estimand and the same stay-at-home construction as the supplied replication code, while its later August outcome provides a temporally distinct replication comparison.
qualification.similarity_to_original: The original study used county-level Unacast mobility, American Community Survey characteristics, and MIT Election Data and Science Lab election data (post_registration.json, original_study.data and original_study.method). The supplied files contain county FIPS, state, daily pop_home/pop_not_home, Trump vote share, income, demographics, industry, and rurality fields (task_input/replication_data/transportation.csv and county_variables.csv).
qualification.deviation_from_original: The original-study summary specifies March 19–28, 2020 relative to a pre-COVID reference week (post_registration.json, original_study.data). The supplied analysis code uses March 19–April 1 and also August 16–29, with a seeded 5% county sample (task_input/replication_data/kavanagh_analysis.R).

data_plan.notes: The supplied code refers to several county-variable names not present in the delivered CSV. The executable maps them to the available percent_male and percent_rural fields and uses the available non-overlapping Census age bands; this is an explicitly documented fidelity limitation.

planned_method.steps: Read transportation data in chunks; compute daily prop_home = pop_home/(pop_home + pop_not_home); average it within county and each specified period; calculate percentage change from the reference period; merge with the seeded county sample; apply listwise deletion; fit separate March and August OLS models with state fixed effects; calculate the Trump-share coefficient and its interquartile-range effect.
planned_method.models: Ordinary least squares with an intercept and state dummy fixed effects.
planned_method.outcome_variable: Percentage-point change in the proportion staying home from the February 16–29 reference period, separately for March and August.
planned_method.control_variables: Per-capita income, sex, race/ethnicity, college attainment, retail/transportation/health-education-social-services employment, rurality, available age-band percentages, and state fixed effects.
planned_method.tools_software: Python 3.11 with pandas, NumPy, SciPy, statsmodels, and matplotlib.

planned_estimation_and_test.estimation: OLS coefficient for Trump vote share and the corresponding effect of a sample interquartile-range increase.
planned_estimation_and_test.test: Two-sided OLS t-test of the Trump-share coefficient, with 95% confidence intervals.

planned_method.missing_data_handling: Listwise deletion after merging, for all outcome, predictor, control, and state fields required by both models.
planned_method.multiple_testing_policy: No multiplicity correction; March is the focal comparison and August is a pre-specified secondary period in the supplied replication code.
planned_method.inference_criteria: The focal hypothesis is supported when the Trump-share coefficient is negative and its two-sided p-value is below 0.05.

files.replication_analysis.py: Executable end-to-end analysis. It reads the supplied CSV inputs using relative paths, constructs period-specific stay-at-home changes in chunks, fits state-fixed-effect OLS models, writes machine-readable results/tables/figure, and prints a concise summary.

codebase.notes: Run from the workspace root with python replication_analysis.py. Results are written to results/.

other: Other necessary software (e.g., git, make, wget)

analysis.instructions: Install requirements, then execute python replication_analysis.py from the workspace root. Inspect results/results.json for numerical outputs and results/model_results.csv, results/ols_march_summary.txt, results/ols_august_summary.txt, and results/trump_share_coefficients.png for supporting outputs.
analysis.comparison_metrics: Compare the sign, p-value, 95% confidence interval, and interquartile-range effect of Trump vote share in the March model with the original claim of a -4.1 percentage-point effect (95% CI -5.2 to -3.0).
